section_header: AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM — Refrigerant Lines, Expansion Valve
title: REPLACEMENT OF REFRIGERANT LINES

content.text: Cap the open fittings immediately to keep moisture out of the system.
Tightening torques for the O-ring fittings.

content.caption: Tightening torques for the O-ring fittings

items: EVACUATE, CHARGE AND TEST REFRIGERATION SYSTEM (See page AC-12)

content.description: Diagram showing charging hose connection setup with connections to refrigeration system, manifold gauge, and compressor. Labels indicate charging hose, connection to refrigeration system, connection to manifold gauge, and connection to compressor.
Diagram showing manifold gauge set with two pressure gauges (LO and HI) and connection points. Shows high and low pressure gauges with connecting hoses.

items: CHECK QUANTITY OF GAS DURING REFRIGERATION CYCLE
(a) Close the high pressure and low pressure valves.
(b) Connect the high pressure hose to the discharge service valve of the compressor.
(c) Connect the low pressure hose to the suction service valve of the compressor.

content.text: Run the engine at 2,000 rpm for at least 5 minutes. Then check that the high pressure reading is 13 – 15 kg/cm² (185 – 213 psi, 1,275 – 1,471 kPa).
If the expansion valve is faulty, the low pressure reading will drop to 0 kg/cm² (0 psi, 0 kPa), otherwise it is OK.
When the low pressure drops to 0 kg/cm² (0 psi, 0 kPa), feel the receiver's IN and OUT sides for no temperature difference.
